chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Dāwūd al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Ṣaghīr, from his grandfather Shuʿayb, from Mufaḍḍal, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: “Whenever the servant increases in iman, he increases in constriction in his livelihood.”

key_terms.إِيمَانًا: faith; the servant’s spiritual belief and conviction
key_terms.ازْدَادَ: increased; grew more in degree or intensity
key_terms.الْعَبْدُ: the servant; the human being in relation to Allah
key_terms.مَعِيشَتِهِ: his livelihood; his worldly means of living

ai.seo_question: Does increased iman lead to hardship in a believer’s livelihood?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that stronger iman may be accompanied by greater hardship in worldly livelihood. It presents material constriction as something that can coincide with spiritual growth rather than contradict it.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Dawood Al Haza’a, from Muhammad Bin Sagheer, from his grandfather Shuayb, from Mufazzal who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Every time the Emān of the servant increases, the constriction in his livelihood increases’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Muhammad ibn Ali from Dawud al-Hadhdha’ from Muhammad ibn Saghir from his grandfather, Shu’ayb from Mufaddal who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘As the belief of a person increases in strength, his poverty intensifies.’”
